strategy: Add one durable, host-independent StarterHostOrchestrator above the existing selection, Starter runtime, TaskRun bridge, and DurableHostSkillBridge. It persists a revisioned session cursor, delegates exact selection/confirmation to starter_runtime, creates exactly one TaskRun bound to the session and resolved Workflow, projects one closed next_action from the canonical runtime status, and permits only the matching Host/external/human resume method. It injects existing Provider adapters, durable checkpointer, and optional WriteAuthorityGuard rather than recreating them.

changes.responsibility: own durable Host-session ordering, one TaskRun binding, runtime reconstruction, exact next-action projection, and legal resume dispatch
changes.reason: the currently separate correct APIs have no cross-call session owner

changes.responsibility: publish the closed persisted session and next-action shape
changes.reason: ChatGPT/Codex wrappers require a versioned reviewable transport contract

changes.responsibility: prove selection, confirmation, TaskRun reuse, repeated Host resume, phase rejection, tamper rejection, and Graph END to VALIDATING
changes.reason: the new session ordering boundary must fail closed

changes.responsibility: document concrete ChatGPT/Codex interaction, extension, resume, authority, and standalone project behavior
changes.reason: operators need one clear embedding sequence above the bridge

changes.responsibility: replace the future-wrapper gap with the orchestrator boundary while retaining transport limitations
changes.reason: the architecture record must match executable coverage

unchanged_boundaries: ChatGPT/Codex remains the semantic interpreter and must select one candidate exposed by the verified Starter
resolve_starter_host_selection remains exact selection and mutating confirmation authority
DurableHostSkillBridge remains per-Skill request/result evidence transport
StarterWorkflowRuntime and LangGraph remain Workflow execution authorities
TaskRun remains lifecycle and completion authority
Capability Resolver and WorkflowAdapterDispatcher retain Provider binding and dispatch ownership
existing WriteAuthorityGuard remains mandatory for mutating Skill or Provider effects
external waits remain event-driven and Human Gates require explicit decisions
Graph END remains VALIDATING and no merge adapter or automatic completion is added
customer application source and runtime dependencies remain unchanged and independently runnable
forbidden_repairs: Do not add a keyword or fuzzy natural-language router.
Do not automatically confirm a mutating selection or treat selection as write authority.
Do not fabricate Host Skill results, tool receipts, Provider receipts, external events, or Human decisions.
Do not create a second graph runtime, TaskRun state machine, write guard, Quality judge, completion controller, or merge path.
Do not restart a session that already started or accept a resume kind unrelated to the active runtime status.
Do not poll external systems or keep the Workflow invocation alive across waits.
Do not modify customer Agent product source, packaging, or runtime dependencies.
required_invariants: session identity binds Host, verified registration, exact user request, resolved entrypoint, Workflow, and one stable TaskRun
session persistence is revisioned and conflicting writers fail closed
mutating selection cannot start before exact effect-preview confirmation and still grants no write authority
a started session cannot create another TaskRun or restart the graph
Host result submission must match the active WAITING_HOST execution identity
external and human resumes are accepted only in their matching runtime phases with durable evidence
next_action is derived only from canonical runtime state and has authority_effect false
Graph END projects EVALUATE_COMPLETION_POLICY with TaskRun VALIDATING, never COMPLETED

focused: read-only natural-language selection starts one TaskRun and yields the exact Host Skill request
multiple Host Skill results resume the same session and TaskRun until Graph END becomes VALIDATING
mutating selection remains AWAITING_CONFIRMATION until an exact preview digest is confirmed
closed next_action values cover Host wait, external wait, Human Gate, validation, and blocked states
counterexamples: wrong session revision, registration, selection request, entrypoint, confirmation digest, TaskRun, Workflow, or Host execution is rejected
start before selection/confirmation, duplicate start, wrong resume kind, missing evidence, and stale runtime state are rejected
session/result tampering and concurrent conflicting persistence are rejected
regression: Starter selection, runtime, Host bridge, TaskRun bridge, Provider adapter, invocation, and authoring suites remain green
complete Skill unit and all required skill-only profiles remain green
negative_path: the orchestrator never interprets free-form language or executes arbitrary Host commands
selection, confirmation, and session identity grant no write authority
no Skill receipt exists before a validated Host result resumes the Skill node
Graph END never marks TaskRun COMPLETED and no merge capability is introduced
standalone customer application source and dependencies remain unchanged

risks: A Host may crash between receiving a next action and submitting evidence; revisioned durable state allows exact resume without blind replay.
Provider credentials and target-specific profile policies remain environment inputs; the orchestrator must block when they are not injected.
The session proves repository-visible ordering and evidence binding, not a model provider's private reasoning.
rollback_plan: Remove the orchestrator module, schema, tests, and architecture record, and restore the bridge document's future-wrapper statement. Existing independent selection, Starter runtime, TaskRun, Provider, and Host bridge APIs continue to function unchanged.
